title: Dr. Dre and Lovine Embraces AI to Create Music and says that 'the only people that see it as a threat are the people who have trouble creating.'"
author: Suspicious_Neck_4069
selftext:
“There will be some crappy music. There’s crappy music now,” Iovine told the NYT. “In the studio, when gifted people have AI, they’re going to make better records.”

Dr. Dre said he uses AI in producing “as a tool to see what it would do with what I just did.”

comments.author: shlaifu
comments.body:
meh. he's rich and famous, AI or not isn't going to affect him. those people who have 'trouble creating' is basically everybody who isn't rich and famous, whose best bet is now, all of a sudden, to prompt an agent to promot 10000 songs a day and dump them on spotify. If you're not famous now, that's your competition and your best bet is to join it to fight over diminishing returns.
probably not what people went into music for.

replies.author: Suspicious_Neck_4069
replies.body: His wealth shields him from the consequences, but it doesn’t cancel out the signal. He faces far less risk than a beginner, yet in an environment where revealing one’s use of AI can trigger a backlash, choosing to own up to it publicly still comes at a cost.

replies.author: shlaifu
replies.body: >His wealth shields him from the consequences

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
Is making stuff just a way of manifesting sexual selection in humans?  What's the obsession with sorting the gifted from the non-gifted?

As a maker of art, I want to enjoy the creation experience, express myself, and maybe reach an audience, maybe even make some money.  I enjoy compliments of my work, but "you're so talented" is a cheap high (that comes with a cost) compared to "I'm so glad I found this" or "this means a lot to me" or "you/your work inspires me"

As a consumer of art, I want to be entertained and learn.  I want experiences that are memorable, worth my time, worth paying for.  I don't really care if the maker was a talented specimen, but I do care if the maker had something to say that I connect with, and I think anyone alive can do that.

replies.author: Felfedezni
replies.body: They just want to deny others the freedom to express themselves however they choose.
